correctness.rationale: The Fourier coefficients are u_n(1+bD_n/2), with D_n=(u_{n-k}+u_{n+k})/u_n and u even. Positivity on finite sites is equivalent to nonnegative Fourier coefficients. For 0<α<1, D_n rises strictly for 0≤n≤k. Beyond k the backward increments a_n=n^α−(n−k)^α are strictly decreasing and convex (they integrate the strictly convex derivative of x^α). Thus a_n−a_{n+1}≥a_{n+k}−a_{n+k+1}>0, and the decrease of exp(ta_n) is larger than the increase of exp(−ta_{n+k}). Only ±k saturate. At α=1, D_n is constant at 2cosh(tk) for n≥k; direct substitution gives the stated positive coefficients on |n|<k and no tail. Consecutive frequencies yield ordinary Vandermonde rank, both for this finite band and for the infinite positive block when α<1. For α>1, the backward increment tends to infinity, so D_n→∞ and every b<0 creates negative modes eventually. The exact threshold and its jump follow.
